items.title: [Fix] moe: Make biased top-k symbolic-shape safe
items.author: rumitdesai
items.summary: The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic. For routing scores shaped and a shared correction bias shaped, the intended operation is: The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic …
items.body:
The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic.

For routing scores shaped `[T, E]` and a shared correction bias shaped `[E]`, the intended operation is:

```text
[T, E] + [1, E]
```

The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic expert width:

`correction_bias.view(-1, num_experts)`

items.title: fix(rocm): drain GPU during MLA fp8 BMM load warmup
items.author: zhenhantech
items.summary: Fixes ROCm model load failures when Aiter Triton fp8 BMM warmup is enabled. MLA layers pre-compile batch sizes 1..1024 in; without draining the caching allocator after async Triton launches, memory use can peak to OOM on MLA-heavy models before load finishes.
items.body:
Sync and periodically empty the caching allocator while pre-compiling fp8 BMM batch sizes 1..1024.



## Overview

Fixes ROCm model **load** failures when Aiter Triton fp8 BMM warmup is enabled
(`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1`). MLA layers pre-compile batch sizes 1..1024 in
`process_weights_after_loading`; without draining the caching allocator after
async Triton launches, memory use can peak to OOM on MLA-heavy models before load
finishes. Forward/inference behavior is unchanged.

**Scope:** `is_aiter_triton_fp8_bmm_enabled` only (ROCm + Aiter fp8 BMM). Default
upstream env keeps fp8 BMM off;

items.title: [Perf] diffusion: Avoid boolean indexing in placeholder validation
items.author: labAxiaoming
items.summary: Boolean indexing adds indexing and gather overhead and can also trigger D2H synchronization on CUDA. Instead, sum the token mask before expand and call.item to retrieve the count.
items.body:
## Motivation

Boolean indexing adds indexing and gather overhead and can also trigger D2H synchronization on CUDA. Instead, sum the token mask before expand and call .item() to retrieve the count. This avoids indexing and gathering while retaining the scalar D2H synchronization.

Count placeholder tokens directly instead. On the reported NVIDIA H800 server, this reduces the isolated counting latency by **15.6–15.7x**. The scalar synchronization from `sum().item()` remains.

## Modifications

- Qwen-VL: replace boolean indexing with `mask[..., 0].sum().item()` for image and video valid

items.title: fix(GTP+PP): Isolate default prefetch chains per virtual pipeline chunk
items.author: fanshiqing
items.summary: Fix silent weight corruption when GTP is used with virtual pipeline parallelism (VPP). Default prefetch registration groups weights by role and process group across all model chunks.
items.body:
# What does this PR do?
Fix silent weight corruption when GTP is used with virtual pipeline parallelism (VPP).

Default prefetch registration groups weights by role and process group across all model chunks. Because virtual chunks execute forward and backward independently, a gather in one chunk can overwrite another chunk's live weight buffer. In the regression, a pending forward weight filled with `3` is overwritten with another chunk's weight filled with `9`.

This change includes model-chunk identity in default chain grouping. Each chunk gets separate dense and grouped-expert FC1/FC2 chain

items.title: [Perf] KDA ReplaySSM: commit a one-token verify in place
items.author: thangquang09
items.summary: With and, high batch sizes run at: the verify carries one token per request, and that token is always accepted. On the KDA ReplaySSM path that verify still writes the ring and leaves untouched, then the commit folds the ring back into.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--speculative-adaptive` and `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, high batch sizes run at `steps=0`: the verify carries one token per request, and that token is always accepted. On the KDA ReplaySSM path that verify still writes the ring and leaves `temporal` untouched, then the commit folds the ring back into `temporal`. Each step reads the fp32 SSM state in the verify, then reads and writes it again in the fold. A plain decode reads and writes it once.

On GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 (TP4, B300), this made a `steps=0` step 7–16% slower than a decode step without speculative decoding

HiCache L3 lookups hash with the JIT-built `hicache_hash_cpp` extension, which needs OpenSSL headers. items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: An L3 prefetch is read by one IO thread per rank, one 128-page batch at a time, and each batch reads the KV pool and then its KV-derived pools (e.g. an indexer) one after the other.
items.body:
## Motivation

An L3 prefetch is read by one IO thread per rank, one 128-page batch at a time, and each batch reads the KV pool and then its KV-derived pools (e.g. an indexer) one after the other. A long L3 hit therefore waits for a chain of serial backend calls even when the backend and NIC have headroom. #45106 fixed the same pattern on the direct linker load path; this PR brings the concurrency part to the HiCache prefetch path.

## Modifications

- New storage extra-config key `prefetch_io_threads` (default `1`, i.e. unchanged behavior). With `N > 1`, one prefetch operation keeps up to `N`

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Use the request's max_slice_nums for MiniCPM-V/O image placeholders
items.author: Jaeyeong-CHOI
items.summary: Fixes engine crash when request-level max_slice_nums mismatches placeholder token count for MiniCPM-V/O multimodal models by reading effective value from request-configured image processor.
items.body:
## Overview

For MiniCPM-V (2.x / 4 / 4.5) and MiniCPM-o, passing `max_slice_nums` per request through `mm_processor_kwargs` crashes the engine. The HF processor applies the request value and produces fewer image crops, but the prompt replacement sizes the image placeholder with the engine-level image processor, so the number of placeholder tokens no longer matches the image embeddings (e.g. 64 embeddings for 192 placeholder tokens) and the engine dies. This PR reads the effective `max_slice_nums` from the request-configured image processor and passes it to the existing placeholder helpers.

## Summary

DeepSeek-V4-Flash requires `swiglu_limit=10`, but batched DeepGEMM's fused activation/FP8 quantization omitted it. This fixes expert computation; it does not change DeepEP transport.

The CUDA implementation specializes clamp/no-clamp at compile time, converts BF16 bounds on the host, and optimizes the existing maximum/prefix reductions to avoid the initial implementation's performance

The Rust frontend is meant to become the default through an `auto` mode: Rust when it can serve the configuration, otherwise Python, decided at startup only. items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Slice NVFP4 KV pages by head in heterogeneous-TP WRITE
items.author: ChengYM5685
items.summary: Fixes MoRIIO heterogeneous-TP WRITE corrupting NVFP4 KV cache on ROCm by slicing pages according to the actual head-major layout instead of the incorrect per-head-contiguous assumption.
items.body:
## Overview

MoRIIO's heterogeneous-TP WRITE corrupts the NVFP4 KV cache of MiniMax-M3 on ROCm (`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`): it cuts the page into per-head slots as if each KV head's bytes were contiguous, but the ROCm page stores all heads' FP4 data before all heads' block scales on each K/V side. A decode instance with a smaller TP than prefill (e.g. TP4 -> TP1) receives scrambled KV and generates garbage. This PR slices those pages by their real layout, and refuses any other packed NVFP4 page instead of mis-slicing it.

## Claims

- Prefill TP != decode TP over MoRIIO WRITE with an NVFP4 KV

## Summary

When several requests reach an idle server together, the overlap scheduler

## Summary

On gfx12 (RDNA4), W4A16 `down_proj`-like layers (large K) at batch 3-5 fall off the fast HIP skinny int4 kernel onto the
Triton fallback, because the HIP path is gated by an LDS size check. The HIP kernel already has a `CHUNKED` variant that
walks K in LDS-sized chunks and removes that limit; it is compiled for all gfx1x but only enabled on gfx115x.

**This PR enables the existing chunked kernel on gfx12.** No new kernel, no new op, no weight-layout change - only the
dispatch rule changes. Result on gfx1201: **1.2-2.45x faster** on the affected GEMMs, same numerics.

items.title: [Fix] rust: Link PyO3 extensions on macOS with dynamic_lookup
items.author: swhsiang
items.summary: On macOS, the Rust extension loader builds PyO3 extensions with a plain, and the link step fails: A PyO3 cdylib leaves the Python C API symbols for the interpreter to resolve at import time. Linux allows that by default.
items.body:
## Motivation

On macOS, the Rust extension loader (`python/sglang/srt/rust_extensions/loader.py`) builds PyO3 extensions with a plain `cargo build`, and the link step fails:

```
error: linking with `cc` failed: exit status: 1
  ... undefined pyo3 symbols such as _PyErr_SetString and _PyExc_ValueError ...
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1
```

A PyO3 cdylib leaves the Python C API symbols for the interpreter to resolve at import time. Linux allows that by default. Apple's linker needs `-undefined dynamic_lookup`, which maturin and setuptools-rust add and plain `cargo build`

items.title: [Perf] disaggregation: Stream a PD decode request's first token with its first decode output
items.author: weireweire
items.summary: A PD decode server streams the prefill-sampled first token as soon as the request is admitted. Under the overlap scheduler, that request's first decode forward is queued behind the forward already in flight, so its next tokens arrive about two decode steps lat…
items.body:
## Motivation

A PD decode server streams the prefill-sampled first token as soon as the request is admitted (`process_batch_result_prebuilt`). Under the overlap scheduler, that request's first decode forward is queued behind the forward already in flight, so its next tokens arrive about two decode steps later.

Client TPOT is computed as (e2e - TTFT) / (osl - 1), so this gap is charged to every request's TPOT. On DeepSeek-V4.1 with DEP32 decode, the time to the second token was ~104 ms, against ~92 ms for a steady 32-token chunk.

items.body:
## Motivation

ComfyUI exports keep the same fused `qkv` tensor shape as official H3 checkpoints but store the rows as `[q_all, k_all, v_all]` instead of head-interleaved. Quantized ComfyUI files are detected from per-layer metadata (ConvRot INT8, W4A8, W4A4, MXFP8, NVFP4, GGUF) and skip the reorder. An unquantized BF16 ComfyUI export carries no markers, so it looks like an official checkpoint, the default head-interleaved reorder runs, and the server renders noise without any error.

items.body:
## Motivation

`EPLBManager` waits `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations` passes before every rebalance, including the first one. Each rebalance pauses serving, so large EP deployments set a long interval. That makes the first rebalance wait just as long, and until then the server runs on the initial (by default trivial) expert layout, which hurts tail latency early on.

This PR adds a separate setting for the first rebalance, so it can come early while later rebalances keep the long interval.

It is complementary to #43754 (stop rebalancing after N rebalances) and #45282 (asynchronous rebalance).

When `SparsePrefillKVBuffer._reserve` grows the DSv4 sparse-prefill scratch, it assigns the new tensor over the old one, so both are alive while `torch.empty` runs. items.title: [Bugfix][Ray] Keep EngineCore's SIGTERM handler across ray.init()
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Restores EngineCore's SIGTERM handler after ray.init, preventing GPU memory leaks from orphaned Ray workers due to skipped graceful shutdown.
items.body:
## Overview

`ray.init()` replaces EngineCore's SIGTERM handler, so a SIGTERM from the frontend skips vLLM's graceful shutdown and Ray's C++ failure handler aborts EngineCore 3 s later. When the abort lands before `RayExecutorV2.shutdown()` kills the actors, the Ray workers outlive the engine and keep their GPU memory. This restores the caller's handler after `ray.init()`.

## Claims

- EngineCore with the Ray backend shuts down through its own SIGTERM handler, aborting requests and killing the Ray actors, instead of `sys.exit()` plus a SIGABRT 3 s later
- No `RayWorkerProc` is left holding

items.author: MatthewBonanni
items.summary: Fixes FlashMLA FP8 sparse decode crashes with HiSparse by reading the hot KV cache as flat rows instead of 64-token pages, correcting stride calculations for interleaved cache layouts.
items.body:
## Purpose

FLASHMLA_SPARSE with HiSparse crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access in the FP8 sparse decode kernel. Before the crash, decode attention reads the wrong KV rows.

HiSparse resolves top-k to flat-row indices over the hot cache: `block * block_stride_rows + offset`. With `fp8_ds_mla`, hot blocks interleave with other layers' rows, so the stride is 271 rows rather than 64. `_host_backed_fp8_decode` passed the strided cache to FlashMLA as 64-token pages, and FlashMLA decodes an index as `page * 64 + offset`. Most indices pointed at the wrong row, and high blocks pointed past the end

CPython 3.11+ keeps frames in per-thread data-stack chunks. When a hot call sits at a chunk boundary, every call maps a fresh chunk and every return unmaps it (gh-142183). CPython fixed this in 3.13.13 and 3.14.4; 3.12 will not get the fix.

Add run_with_frame_stack_reserve() and call PyExecutor.event_loop through it, so the loop starts n

## Overview

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the MXFP4 linear kernel selector on CUDA could pick Marlin, whose output for a row changes with the batch size. This PR does for MXFP4 what #67806 did for MXFP8: the MXFP4 linear kernels get a `supports_batch_invariance()` capability and, in batch-invariant mode, kernels without it are dropped before selection. Related: #27433, #65560.

- With the flag on, MXFP4 linear layers on CUDA only run on kernels that declare batch invariance: FlashInfer, Humming and Emulation, in the existing priority order.

items.summary: Retain cached eager packing and use GPU-generated metadata for attention graph warmup and capture, supporting changed packed boundaries within fixed-size buffers. Full-GRPO speedup remains unverified.
items.body:
## Functionality
Add opt-in chunkwise GDN context parallelism for TP1 training without sequence parallelism. Retain cached eager packing and use GPU-generated metadata for attention graph warmup and capture, supporting changed packed boundaries within fixed-size buffers.

## Speedup
The combined chunkwise path achieved **+6.25% policy-training throughput** in a Qwen3.5-397B prototype benchmark (32 GB300 GPUs, CP4, GBS512, synthetic rollouts). Full-GRPO speedup remains unverified.

items.author: NickLucche
items.summary: Fixes infinite retry loop in MooncakeStore where failed remote KV loads bounce requests between WAITING states instead of falling back to local recompute.
items.body:
## Purpose

With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a failed MooncakeStore load resets `num_computed_tokens` and reschedules the request, and the scheduler clears its failure marker once the receive completes. On the next admission `MooncakeStoreScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens` queries the store again; if the lookup keeps reporting the hit while the GET keeps failing (e.g. stale metadata for a dead segment), the request bounces between `WAITING` and `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever and never falls back to local compute.

## Motivation

Refs #50547. PD currently requires prefill to run the LM head and provide the first sampled token, even when request sampling state belongs on decode.

Decode extends the remaining prompt in its already allocated slots and samples the first output token. Short prompts use a metadata-only handoff. The default value zero retains the existing path.

## Description

Closes #22350.

The eager MTP metadata update reads a CUDA accepted-token scalar for each decode request before updating the host KV lengths. A mixed prefill/decode batch can take this path even when graphs are configured. Transfer the active decode slice once and update the existing host list in place. CUDA graph batches retain the existing device-only behavior.

## Validation

The exact production method was tested on one NVIDIA L20 using PyTorch 2.10.0+cu129 and CUDA 12.9. The test uses real CUDA tensors and a lightweight metadata fixture, with no model or executor startup.

items.title: fix(benchmarks): use platform FP8 dtype in the MoE tuner quant config
items.author: Wilson0511
items.summary: Fixes hardcoded FP8 dtype mismatch in MoE tuner benchmark on FNUZ platforms by passing FP8_DTYPE through to the quant config.
items.body:
## FIX

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` in the `use_fp8_w8a8` branch of the quant-config setup, while the expert weights a few lines above are cast with `FP8_DTYPE` (= `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`). On FNUZ platforms (gfx942) the two disagree, `FusedMoEQuantConfig.use_fp8_w8a8` evaluates False, and `--dtype fp8_w8a8` tuning dies in the unquantized path.

This PR passes `FP8_DTYPE` through, keeping the quant config consistent with the weight casts. AST regression tests cover the fp8 / int8 / unquantized branches without importing torch.

Cuts the Muse bf16 MoE block time on Hopper by up to 20% at EP8 by running the fused post-expert kernel at every batch size.

items.body:
ptxas through CUDA 13.2 can silently miscompile register-input wgmma, so this refuses any JIT build whose SASS it got wrong.

The bug lets code after a register-input wgmma overwrite that wgmma's A registers while it is still in flight. The wrong answers depend on timing, so tests rarely catch them. items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Stages non-contiguous and dtype-converted weight copies through pinned memory in copy_weight_, eliminating unowned GPU memory leaks during checkpoint loading on NVIDIA Grace.

## Purpose

On Grace (ATS), when the GPU reads the same pageable anonymous host pages many times, the UVM driver allocates GPU memory in 128 MiB units. - sources that `copy_()` stages itself (non-contiguous or dtype-converting), e.g. routed-expert `w13` shards;

items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Locks worker pageable GPU memory via mlockall to prevent page-table access-flag aging, reducing first-wake checkpoint restore from 16–24 s to ~6 s on Grace/ATS platforms.
items.body:
## Purpose

On Grace (ATS), the GPU reads host memory through the CPU page tables. Under host memory pressure, reclaim ages the workers' unlocked pages by clearing the access flag in their page-table entries. CUDA checkpoint Restore then revisits the registered host memory, and every aged page takes a fault that flushes the TLB. Each flush sends a synchronous SMMU and GPU ATC invalidation. On GB300, the first wake after startup took 16–24 s instead of about 6 s. items.summary: spawns threads, each entering around. → temporarily rewrites the process-global executable (and mutates ).
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix a race in automatic NUMA binding when local workers start concurrently.

`_start_workers_concurrently()` spawns `local_world_size` threads, each entering `numa_utils.configure_subprocess()` around `proc.start()`. `configure_subprocess` → `_mp_set_executable` temporarily rewrites the **process-global** `multiprocessing.spawn` executable (and `_set_numa_wrapper_env` mutates `os.environ`). Two overlapping threads interleave set/assert/restore, and the exit assertion in `_mp_set_executable` fires:

```
AssertionError: Executable was changed during NUMA binding context: expected

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

items.title: [#22228][fix] Draw trtllm-bench output lengths independently of input lengths
items.author: sohailshk
items.summary: Fixes #22228 and seeded the input-length and the output-length generators with the same, so both lengths were drawn from the same random sequence and every request's output length followed its input length (correlation 1.0). The output lengths now use.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22228

`token-norm-dist` and `token-unif-dist` seeded the input-length and the output-length generators with the same `--random-seed`, so both lengths were drawn from the same random sequence and every request's output length followed its input length (correlation 1.0). items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.title: Compute DSA split gradient norms from DTensor layouts in FullyShardedOptimizer
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

A DeepSeek-V4 Pro proxy on 64 GB200 with MFSDP v2 now runs past the first step.

### What does this PR do?

`PPOTrainer._compute_old_log_prob` (v1) always sends `calculate_entropy=True` to `compute_log_prob`. Entropy over the full vocabulary is expensive: on the TorchTitan TPU engine it is a chunked pass over 248k logits per token. The trainer then pulls the `entropy` field back from TransferQueue, pads it, and writes it back. The only thing that uses it is the `actor/entropy` metric. `_update_actor` already skips entropy when `entropy_coeff == 0`.

This PR makes `old_log_prob` follow the existing actor config. Entropy is computed only when `actor_rollout_ref.actor.calcula

items.title: [ckpt, ray] fix: scope checkpoint collectives to the worker device
items.author: ETOgaosion
items.summary: The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device.
items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.title: Add `--logits-dtype` to keep Megatron actor logits in bf16
items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [Bug][Training] Colocated online DSpark training never updates the draft: update_weights() replaces its parameters' storage
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: In colocated runs (, so ), online DSpark draft training never changes the draft. The trainer computes the draft loss and its gradients and steps the optimizer, but the draft that is trained, backed up and served to vLLM stays the pretrained one.
items.body:
## Summary

In colocated runs (`--colocate`, so `offload_train`), online DSpark draft training never changes the draft. The trainer computes the draft loss and its gradients and steps the optimizer, but the draft that is trained, backed up and served to vLLM stays the pretrained one. items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: chaoworks
items.summary: Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer …
items.body:
Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer scan every safetensors file, so a stale file visited last can override the indexed tensor location. ## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.body: ### Summary Based on the RFC [315](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/315) , add support for building images. ### Changes 1、Add a run-npu-ci-image-build option to NPU CI. When this option is selected, it will rebuild the image, and all subsequent test cases will run using the newly built image. 2、Modify dockerfile.npu to enable caching during the image build step, which accelerates the build process. ### Test result
